featured_reviews.name: Sagar Jondhale
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Malhar recently for lunch and ordered a variety of dishes, including Crab Lollipop, Prawns Koliwada, White Rice, Rava Bombil, and Agri-style Chicken Curry. We had also planned to try Amboli and Bhakri, but unfortunately, both were out of stock.

The Crab Lollipop and Prawns Koliwada were flavorful and well-prepared. However, the Agri-style Chicken Curry did not meet expectations. The use of garam masala was overpowering, and the excessive black pepper (kalimiri) affected the overall taste, though the dish was still edible.

The ambience of the restaurant was very beautiful, but I noticed some issues with cleanliness. For example, one of the glasses provided still had food particles stuck on the edge where a person drinks. I requested the steward to replace the glass; he took the dirty one but forgot to bring a new glass altogether, leaving me to drink directly from the bottle.

While the food was average overall, I was particularly disappointed with the service. Both the steward and the captain seemed uninterested and inattentive. Despite repeated requests, it took them over 15 minutes to bring tissues, even when asked clearly and politely.

Additionally, the Prawns Koliwada was served nearly 40 minutes later, after we had almost finished our main course. At that time, only 3–4 tables were occupied in the restaurant, so such a delay was unjustified. When I raised this issue with the captain, his casual response was, "Humare yaha thoda late hi hota hai." This type of attitude is not expected from a reputed establishment like Malhar.

In summary, although the ambience was nice and some dishes were good, the poor service, lack of attention to cleanliness, and indifferent staff attitude significantly impacted our overall dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Sumit K
featured_reviews.review_text:
Aswad Restaurant is an excellent place for anyone looking to enjoy authentic Maharashtrian vegetarian food in a clean, comfortable, and welcoming environment in dadar mumbai. The restaurant maintains very high standards of hygiene, which adds greatly to the overall dining experience.

The food is not only delicious but also very affordable, making it a great option for regular meals as well as for first-time visitors wanting to explore traditional Maharashtrian cuisine. Their **Maharashtrian thali** is highly recommended, offering a wholesome and satisfying combination of flavors. Special dishes like **Bhakri–Pithla** and **Thalipeeth** are prepared perfectly and taste truly homely.

One of the highlights of Aswad is their **Modak**, which is simply the best—fresh, flavorful, and a must-try for dessert lovers. The food is mild, not overly spicy or oily, making it suitable for all age groups and ideal for those who prefer healthy, home-style meals.

The service is polite, prompt, and courteous, adding to the pleasant atmosphere of the restaurant. Its convenient location near **Dadar Metro Station** makes it easily accessible in mumbai.

Overall, Aswad Restaurant is a wonderful choice for hygienic, affordable, and authentic Maharashtrian vegetarian food with a comforting, home-cooked feel. Highly recommended.

featured_reviews.review_text:

We started off with Paneer Pahadi Kabab and Chicken Laasooni Kabab – both were packed with flavors and perfectly cooked. For the main course, we tried Smokey Butter Chicken and Mushroom Masala paired with chapati and steamed rice. The butter chicken especially stood out – rich, creamy, and truly a treat.

To end the meal on a sweet note, we had Shahi Tukda and Sizzling Brownie with Vanilla Ice Cream. The sizzling brownie was the ultimate showstopper – warm, gooey, and indulgent.

Overall, great food + good vibes = highly recommended! Definitely a must-visit spot in Dadar, especially since it’s right next to the famous Dadar Flower Market

featured_reviews.name: Tanishka Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text:

It’s a cozy dining spot that starts serving snacks from 8 AM and goes on till late drinks at 1 AM, which makes it perfect for any time of the day. The place is divided into two sections, making it ideal for families, couples, or even large groups.

The menu is quite versatile, but their Chinese and South Indian dishes really stand out. I tried the LIIT and Piña Colada, both refreshing and well-balanced. For starters, the Prawns Koliwada and Chicken Sholay Kebab were full of flavor and cooked perfectly.

In mains, the Chicken Bhuna with Tandoor Roti was a comforting combination and absolutely delicious. Ended the meal with a Caramel Pudding, which was the perfect sweet note to finish on.

Overall, the food, service, and ambiance all come together beautifully at Dadar Retreat. Definitely a must-visit spot if you’re in the area!

Pritam Da Dhaba is one of those places that truly lives up to its reputation. Yes, it is quite expensive compared to regular dhabas, but once you taste the food, you understand why people keep coming back.
The ambience has a classic dhaba vibe with a comfortable and well-maintained setup, making it perfect for family dinners as well as outings with friends. The service is quick, polite, and well managed, even during rush hours, which adds a lot to the overall experience.
Coming to the food — this is where Pritam Da Dhaba really shines. The Punjabi flavours are rich, authentic, and full of taste. The gravies are perfectly spiced, buttery, and cooked to perfection. Every dish feels fresh and well prepared, and the quality of ingredients is clearly noticeable. Portion sizes are decent, and the presentation is neat.
Although the pricing is on the higher side, the taste, consistency, and overall dining experience make it worth the money. It’s not an everyday spot, but definitely a place you visit when you want to treat yourself to good Punjabi food.
Overall, Pritam Da Dhaba is expensive but absolutely worth it for the taste, quality, and experience. Highly recommended for anyone who enjoys authentic Punjabi cuisine and doesn’t mind paying a little extra for it. 🌟🍽️

featured_reviews.review_text:
Hello viewer, thank you for passing by to read the review.
We decided to try out some authentic Maharashtrian cuisine and Trupt Potoba Veg Restaurant at Dadar definitely scored on all fronts.
We intended to have their Maharashtrian thali but when tried their various starters, snacks and cool drinks, we were fully stuffed.
We would definitely recommend that you visit with your family (we are surely going to visit again) for the authentic Maharashtrian taste, very good food quality, and hospitality of the staff.
Cost wise the rates seem expensive but for the quality and quantity it is good.
Quick ratings:
Food quality (freshness and ingredients): 5/5
Food taste and authenticity: 5/5
Ambience: 4.5/5
Staff behaviour: 5/5
Service: 4.5/5
Value for money: 4.5/5

For the foodie in you who wishes to know more.... let's dive into individual item reviews that we had.
1. Sabudana vada: 5/5, taste was good. Outer surface slightly crisp and inner was properly cooked. Was served with sweet curd and coconut chutney. Worth a second serving.
2. Bhajaniche Vade combined with Kala Vatana Usual: 5/5, freshly done, balanced taste and vade were soft like puris (not the hard ones). Also they were not oily. Definitely a recommendation.
3. Misal Pav: 4/5, the dish came with kala vatana usal, farsan, onion & lemon, 2 pav, extra kat, buttermilk small portion. The misal was medium spicy and palatable for the normal eaters. What we felt a bit down was the kat, which should be very spicy, but it was normal and same as the vatana usal. So there is scope for improvement on this small part.
4. Mix Marathi snacks (snacks platter): 5/5, very good. Contained two pieces each of batata vada, alu vadi, kothimbir vadi and samosa. Definitely recommend giving a second round.
5. Solkadhi: 5/5, good taste including that of ginger and hing.

I recently visited Trupt Potoba in Mumbai after hearing a lot about its authentic Maharashtrian food—and I must say, it exceeded my expectations. I specially traveled from Pune just to try their food, and it was absolutely worth it. The taste is top-notch—rich, traditional, and comforting, just like homemade meals.

The quality and quantity of food are impressive, and the service is quick and efficient. The hotel staff is very polite and courteous, which adds to the warm dining experience. The restaurant is neat and clean, maintaining good hygiene throughout. A special touch I loved was the soft Marathi music playing in the background—it created a peaceful and cultural ambiance that enhanced the authenticity of the place.

Weekends, usually a wait time of around 10–15 minutes, which is understandable given the popularity. The only improvement I’d suggest is regarding the space—it feels a bit small and could benefit from a bigger seating area.

Overall, Trupt Potoba is one of the best places in Mumbai for Maharashtrian cuisine. Whether it’s Misal, Pithla-Bhakri, or Ukadiche Modak , Varous Thalis & so on —you’ll get the real taste of Maharashtra !

Jay Maharashtra 🚩

featured_reviews.review_text:
After hearing about Kurry Kulture from my friend for almost 2 years, I finally got the chance to visit her husband's restaurant—and it was absolutely worth the wait!

The cleanliness was impressive, right from the dining area to the washroom. The food presentation was top-notch, and the staff was always ready with recommendations to help us choose their best dishes.

We tried the Paneer Pataya, their new starter, the Stuffed Mushroom with spinach and cheese stuffing, and the unique Veg Lollipop made with baby corn instead of a stick, so the entire dish can be enjoyed with zero waste. For the main course, the Veg Maharaja with koftas was absolutely delicious. The Schezwan Fried Rice was another highlight—made without ajinomoto or artificial colours, making it a healthier option for Chinese food lovers. We ended our meal with the unique Ramesh Suresh dessert.

What stood out the most was how flavorful and satisfying the vegetarian food was. As someone who usually prefers non-veg dishes, this meal genuinely made me appreciate and enjoy veg food even more!

They also have party props and organise various events making the experience lively and enjoyable. The menu is extensive, covering Indian, Chinese, Italian, Continental, and much more.

There are so many options that you simply can't try everything in one visit—which gives you every reason to keep coming back.
Great food, excellent hospitality, amazing cleanliness, and a memorable overall experience. Highly recommended!🥳♥️✨🧿

If you're nearby in Tilak Nagar, make sure to visit and experience it for yourself. Wishing them continued success and many more happy customers ahead. 🤭🔥

featured_reviews.name: Shradha Gaikwad
featured_reviews.review_text:
Golden Lawn, located opposite Fine Art, offers a well-balanced experience with its spacious open-air lawn area and a comfortable indoor seating space. The lawn section is particularly attractive, featuring a large theatre-style screen where ongoing matches are telecast, making it a perfect hangout spot for sports lovers. The ambience is vibrant, with well-lit surroundings, neat premises, and helpful staff, ensuring guests feel welcome.

The hotel serves both beverages and food, with options for vegetarian and non-vegetarian platters. Complimentary peanuts and crackers are served with drinks, which adds to the experience. The beverage menu is quite diverse – we tried a Blue Lagoon, Sex on the Beach, and beer – all well-prepared. On the food front, we ordered Chicken Banjara. While the dish was well-cooked, the flavours leaned towards the milder side, not as spicy as expected. The good part is that the kitchen seems to prepare dishes fresh, which may also explain the slightly longer preparation time.

Pricing is slightly on the higher side considering the location, but the quality, ambience, and service justify it. it was a satisfying experience. I’d recommend trying their Mutton Curry, neer dosa  which is said to be their speciality.

featured_reviews.name: Silford Braganza
featured_reviews.review_text:
The place has an awesome ambiance. Outdoor sitting and good lights.

The best feature of the place is the uncle who sings Gazhals. Nothing like a rainy evening and a whiskey in hand and listening to Gazhals. It's the highlight of the place.

The food is decent and they mostly specialise in tandoor.

We ordered the chicken tandoori which fine. Butter chicken is textbook so it's the same like you get it everywhere. We had a clear chicken soup which was good.

The mocktails are good and well priced. It tastes good.

The place is a little expensive, and it gets a little noisy when there's a party. But otherwise it's an ideal for a family gathering or a date night. Indoors or outdoors.
